transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. My name is Primitive Nomad and I'm going to give
you some starting tips and tricks to help you begin your journey in Ash and Fall. In the bottom left of your screen,
you'll see your survival meters: hydration, sustenance, as well as rest. Each one of these affects your character
differently. Hydration affects your stamina recovery, so keeping your water high means you'll recover stamina a lot
faster. Sustenance is your hunger meter. Keeping it filled improves your natural health regeneration and at zero
sustenance, your health will start draining. Although it will not directly kill you unless you're on hard mode. If
you're playing normal, it'll stop at one health. Rest is your fatigue meter. The longer you go without resting, the more
your character's overall performance is affected across the board. Now, your overall survivability is connected to
what is called your power level. Your power level is directly tied to the armor you're currently wearing. And keep
in mind, if you're wearing armor of different power levels, their values are averaged and rounded down to give you
your final level. Now, each region you progress through in Dragon Wilds increases in power. For the most part,
you'll be fighting in regions one power level higher than your current gear until you unlock the recipes and
materials to match that region's power level. Now, if you do go too far, you're going to be under-leveled for that
region. You'll know when this occurs because enemies will indicate this with a skull next to their names, indicating
that they're two or more power levels higher than you. Now, on top of your basic gear set, skills are probably the
most important progression system in Dragon Wilds. Skills cover every aspect of the game. Things like combat,
gathering, crafting, building, farming, cooking, and movement through agility. Skills will level up naturally as you
play, like cutting down trees, mining ore deposits, building your base, as well as using different combat styles
like melee, ranged, and magic all develop the related skill. As you level up skills, you're going to be unlocking
passive bonuses along the way, recipes, equipment, building pieces, and new abilities and skill spells. Skill spells
are special abilities connected to individual skills. Some help in combat, while others make gathering, traveling,
farming, and building a lot easier. Be sure to open the skills menu regularly to check your progress and new unlocks.
There might be a skill spell that you're close to unlocking that will assist you in gathering, exploration, as well as
combat. Now, in order to use these skills, you have to understand the magic of Ashan Fall. The two main sources of
this magic are Anima and Rune Essence. Rune Essence can be gathered by mining Rune Essence Stones surrounding geysers
around Ashan Fall. Some spawn with rocks on the ground that you can easily gather
with your pickaxe, as well as some have floating rocks, which require being hit out of the sky. This is most easily done
with an arrow or an attack from a staff. They will then fall to the ground and you can mine those as well. Now, when
you collect Rune Essence for the first time, this will unlock a crafting station called the Rune Altar. This
crafting station is used to craft runes, which are the resource required to cast all your spells. There are seven
different type of runes in Dragon Wilds. These are used for casting combat magic,
as well as utilizing your utility spells that you will eventually unlock. Spells like Wind Step, helping you with
traversal, Astral Projection, assisting you in wood cutting, and Rock Explosion, speeding up your mining. Now, once you
unlock a skill spell, keep in mind you do have to place it on your spell wheel, as well as make sure you're carrying the
required runes in order to cast that spell. Like I said, there's so many different runes in the title, and many
of these runes are associated with your ability to cast certain spells, so keep that in mind before going out. Now, the
awesome thing about Dragon Wilds, you do not need to grind one skill immediately.
Following the main quest line, gathering resources, crafting equipment, exploring the world of Ashan Fall is passively
going to upgrade all your skills naturally. Now, I recommend when you first jump in, you follow the opening
quest before wandering too far. This early quest line with the old man will introduce the game's main systems and
lead you towards important early game unlocks. Now, recipes are a huge part of your progression in Dragon Wilds, and
there's a few different ways you'll unlock these. The first is by discovering new materials, so as you're
exploring different areas and new resources, you'll naturally start unlocking new crafting possibilities
every time you pick up a new resource. The second is by creating new crafting stations. Different crafting stations
are responsible for different types of progression. For example, a station focused on metalworking will unlock
different recipes compared to a station focused on range weapons, armor, or magic. If you find a new material but
don't see anything new to craft, you may need to bring it to the correct crafting bench or unlock the station that uses
it. Keep in mind there are plenty of chests hidden around Ashen Fall. These chests hold basic items for the region
as well as the potential of getting new decoration items, recipes, and vestiges. These vestiges are also located in many
loot pools around Ashen Fall from basic enemies, world bosses, as well as plenty of other sources. And these are the big
gear chase items in Dragon Wilds. This being a survival game, your base is going to be your main hub for crafting,
cooking, farming, repairing your gear, and preparing yourself in between exploring Ashen Fall. The first thing
you're going to want to place down is your bed and interact with it to turn it into your spawn point. If you die at any
time, this is where you will respawn in the world. Now, while at your base, you'll notice a coziness perk at the
bottom left of your screen. This is tied to your claimed bed. When you're near your bed, your survival meters like
sustenance, thirst, and rest drain much more slowly. This gives you plenty of time to build, organize your base, craft
new equipment, and prepare for your next trip without constantly worrying about your meters dropping. When you do leave
your base, the coziness perk will remain active for an extra 4 minutes, allowing you a buffer when you start your next
adventure. With all that being said, one of the biggest early game tips I can give you is to start investing in
farming and cooking as soon as you can. These two skills work together and become one of the most important parts
of your survival in Dragon Wilds. Food and drinks are not only used to fill your sustenance as well as thirst
meters, but this is also your main source of healing as well as gaining special buffs. Farming gives you a
consistent source of ingredients, while cooking turns those ingredients into stronger meals that can help you explore
further, survive tougher fights, and prepare for bosses. Early on, you will rely on whatever food you can find while
exploring, but eventually you will want to move towards growing your own crops and creating a reliable food supply at
your base. Now, overall, with Dragon Isles being a survival game, be sure to pick up everything you find out in the
open world. All materials will come in handy even in later regions. And be sure you test out different combat styles as
well as elemental types because some enemies are weak or resilient to certain elements. And explore every nook and
cranny because you might not know what you will find out in the world of Ashenfall. It's just a quick breakdown
on all the systems in RuneScape Dragon Isles. So, whether you're jumping into Dragon Isles after experiencing its
early access or you're coming to the title for the first time on its 1.0 launch on September 15th, I hope some of
these tips and tricks helped you out. If you enjoyed the video, drop a like on it and subscribe for all things Dragon
Isles. That's what we do here. We'd love to have you. And as always, guys, stay happy, stay hyped, and have a beautiful
day.
